2. FIDELITY: For each factual claim in the file — dates (e.g. "ruffles.zimmermann.com confirmed 2026-06-09", "Inside Chat direct head tag confirmed 2026-07-10", "MuleSoft PDFs Jun 2025", data-dictionary "~mid-Aug 2026"), requirement IDs (CRM-165–167, PRD-067, REG-051, AAB-004/005, GC-042/060/061, CAI-023, DMU-042, CRM-066–068, etc.), owners, and open-vs-confirmed status — does it match the source exactly? 4. OMISSIONS: Are there open items/unresolved dependencies in openItems.md or projectState.md that are NOT represented in the target file (and arguably should be)?
5. COUNT CHECK: The file claims "42 items across 19 workstreams (41 integration items + data dictionary)". openItems.md claims "41 items across 18 integrations". Verify these counts by actually counting, and confirm the arithmetic/claim is correct.
6. ATTRIBUTION: The file has a "Doc-integrity notes" section citing SFCC-173/SFCC-174 and a return-window CRM-066–068 dependency and a Sparro-vs-Tell-No-Lies attribution issue. Verify the codebase basis for these claims (sparroSchema.md, returns.md, dataMigrationSeo.md).

Do NOT check Confluence or Jira — the parent is handling those separately. Focus only on codebase alignment.

REPORT FORMAT: Return a structured findings list. For each finding: severity (HIGH=factual error/fabrication, MED=stale/misframed, LOW=minor/omission), the exact quote or line from the target file, what the source actually says (with file path + line), and a one-line verdict. End with a short summary: is the file faithful to the codebase or not, and the top 3-5 things to fix. Be precise and cite line numbers. Do not fix anything — report only.
